news.full_article_text: CPI(M) demand judicial probe into 200 MW power purchase in Keralam Thiruvananthapuram, A judicial inquiry has been demanded into the procurement of 200 MW of electricity by the UDF government in October, amid allegations of large-scale corruption and a huge loss to the state exchequer. CPI state secretary M V Govindan alleged on Sunday that corruption had taken place in the deal, while Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan accused the government of purchasing power at a higher rate without following prescribed procedures. Speaking to reporters, Govindan said the electricity was procured at higher rates without inviting tenders or obtaining the necessary approvals from the Electricity Regulatory Commission and other authorities. The purchase was made under emergency provisions without proper consultation, he said. "This is a serious and dangerous development. All files related to the procurement should be made available to the public to ensure transparency," he said. He referred to differences between the electricity minister and the chief minister over the issue, which, he said, had become public. Demanding a judicial inquiry, Govindan said the chief minister was involved in the decision-making process and that an independent investigation was necessary to bring out the facts. In a Facebook post, Vijayan alleged that the government had purchased 200 MW of electricity from VEH Global at ₹ 11 per unit without a tender or approval from the commission. He said he had raised allegations of corruption in the deal in a statement on November 10 and that further details had since emerged. Under Sections 62 and 63 of the Electricity Act, power procurement prices must be determined through procedures approved by the commission or through competitive bidding, Vijayan said. However, the decision to purchase electricity from VEH Global in October was based solely on offers, and the commission had not yet approved the arrangement, he alleged. He pointed out that wind power was available at ₹ 3-4 per unit, while the government had agreed to purchase electricity at ₹ 11 per unit, resulting in a huge loss to the exchequer. Vijayan said the government had accepted VEH Global's offer to supply electricity during peak hours on September 22. He alleged that the government's earlier orders had stated that the company was not eligible to participate in the tender for electricity supply. "Who was interested in awarding the contract to a company that was not eligible?" he asked. He demanded that the chief minister give the public a clear explanation of the alleged irregularities. news.full_article_text: Bengal BJP leader dies after alleged assault by party workers in Panihati: Cop The incident comes amid repeated warnings from senior BJP leaders and ministers that party workers and leaders involved in organised crime A local Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader died in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas district on Saturday night after he was allegedly assaulted by members of a rival group within the party when he intervened in a dispute involving his wife, police said. Arup Saha, the husband of BJP’s local mandal (unit) secretary Ruma Saha, was allegedly assaulted after he came to her rescue during an altercation with a group of party workers in Panihati. Ruma had intervened when the group allegedly assaulted a local trader, Shankar Dey. Arup later complained of chest pain and was taken to Sagar Dutta Medical College and Hospital, where he died, his wife said. “Arup Saha, the deceased, was the husband of the BJP’s local mandal secretary Ruma Saha. People are alleging that Arup went to rescue his wife when she was verbally abused by rival group members for trying to save a trader from their assault. Nobody, however, lodged any complaint till Sunday morning,” a district police officer said, requesting anonymity. Ruma Saha said she intervened after hearing that followers of a BJP youth wing leader were assaulting the trader. “I went to the rescue of a trader when I heard that followers of a BJP youth wing leader were assaulting him. These people surrounded me and verbally abused me. They hit my husband when he intervened. He complained of chest pain after we returned home and died at Sagar Dutta Medical College and Hospital,” she said. Shankar Dey said, “I fell on the ground when they hit me. The BJP workers surrounded Ruma Saha when she tried to stop them.” Ruma Saha alleged that the assailants were followers of Nirmal Ghosh, a former Trinamool Congress MLA from Panihati who faces multiple criminal charges and was recently released on bail. Ghosh is also an accused in the rape and murder case involving the daughter of BJP MLA Ratna Debnath at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in 2024. Ghosh could not be contacted despite several attempts. Debnath, who won the Panihati assembly seat for the BJP in May, told the media that “unwanted elements” continued to operate within the party despite repeated warnings. “I earlier requested the government to intervene. Politicians involved in illegal activities during the Trinamool Congress regime are still active in Panihati,” she said. The incident comes amid repeated warnings from senior BJP leaders and ministers that party workers and leaders involved in organised crime, including extortion, would face action. State BJP leaders have also alleged that Trinamool Congress leaders and their followers who joined the BJP after the assembly elections on May 4 continued to engage in extortion and intra-party violence. West Bengal finance minister Swapan Dasgupta admitted on Saturday that extortion continued under the BJP government. “Extortion is like the new normal. People’s confidence in the administration cannot be restored until it ends. I have stopped some extortions in my constituency but we have not been able to end it fully,” Dasgupta said. On Friday, BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya issued a warning at an event organised by the party’s women’s wing. He alleged that some police personnel were tacitly supporting illegal activities. “Some (BJP) mandal presidents are thinking they are the police and some police personnel are thinking they are the mandal presidents. No lawlessness will be allowed. Identify those who are tarnishing the party and its flag and file FIRs (first information reports). “Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari is also in charge of the police department. I am there too. Give me the papers and I will ensure that these people land in jail,” Bhattacharya said. The Trinamool Congress said Bhattacharya might have good intentions but the law and order situation had deteriorated under the BJP government. Kalyan Banerjee, a senior lawyer and five-time Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MP from Sreerampur in Hooghly district, questioned how complaints could be registered if the police refused to accept them. “Samik may have good intentions but how can an FIR be filed if the police do not accept complaints?” he said. “I can cite an instance from Sreerampur. A woman was molested by BJP workers who also extorted money from her, but the police told her that it was impossible for them to register her complaint,” Banerjee alleged. In a separate incident on Saturday, Koustav Bagchi, the BJP MLA from Barrackpore in North 24 Parganas district, had two people arrested for allegedly selling domestic LPG cylinders illegally in his constituency. “People who ran illegal businesses and gambling dens in Barrackpore during the Trinamool regime are still active,” Bagchi said after facing a demonstration by some BJP workers.

news.full_article_text: 'Damdar Dalit': Akhilesh Yadav gives new spin to Samajwadi Party's PDA coinage He said the 'D' in the party's 'PDA' coinage, which stands for 'pichhda' (backward classes), Dalit, and alpsankhyak (minorities) -- now stands for Damdar Dalit. The Dalit has now become 'damdar (assertive)', Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said on Sunday as he attributed a new meaning to the party's 'PDA' formulation during his address at a 'Dalit Sammelan' here, and described the gathering as the beginning of a broader movement for the upliftment of marginalised communities. Taking a swipe at the BJP, he said those who have considered Agra their stronghold would soon lose their foothold. "This time, the Dalit community will defeat the BJP; wipe them out for good," he asserted. Thanking party MP Ramji Lal Suman and other leaders for organising the event, Yadav said the 'D' in the party's 'PDA' coinage -- which stands for 'pichhda' (backward classes), Dalit, and alpsankhyak (minorities) -- now represents "Damdar Dalit". "Looking at the support of the Dalit community, I can say that the 'D' in our 'PDA', has now become 'Damdar Dalit'," he said. Yadav claimed the BJP is conspiring against the 'PDA' after its electoral defeat in the recent bypolls. Also Read: HT Exclusive: 'Add one to 180', says Akhilesh Yadav on ally Congress's seat demand for UP assembly polls Targeting the ruling party over alleged atrocities against Dalits, he claimed Uttar Pradesh has recorded the highest number of cases of such atrocities, citing National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data. He further alleged that around 200 statues of Dr B R Ambedkar had been vandalised in the state over the past decade. "No action has been taken against those responsible." Yadav said the Samajwadi Party has published a newsletter documenting such incidents of vandalism, including details of where they took place and those allegedly responsible. "Those who vandalise Dr Ambedkar's statues do not merely attack the sculpture. They attack the Constitution held in Babasaheb's hand," he said. "If there is a Constitution, there is dignity. If there is a Constitution, there are rights. If there is a Constitution, there is democracy. And it is democracy that keeps the Constitution alive," he asserted, alleging the BJP's allegiance to "Man Vidhan (anarchy)" instead of the 'Samvidhan' (Constitution). Yadav claimed that the massive turnout at the event reflected growing support for the party's political campaign. He also questioned the claims of the "double-engine" government. "Those who used to talk about double-engine government have been handed a double zero in Kashi," he said, referring to the loss of the BJP candidate from Varanasi in the recent legislative council election. Taking a swipe at Union Home Minister Amit Shah 's recent remarks likening the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh to "Angad ka paon (Angad's foot)", an idiom for immovable, Yadav said the ruling party would soon lose its "footing". "Those who are saying that this government is 'Angad ka paon' will lose their footing. When there is no ground left, where will they place 'Angad ka paon'?" he said. In an apparent jibe at AIMIM chief and Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi, Yadav said some "political tourists" have started arriving in Uttar Pradesh after the BJP's electoral defeats in assembly bypolls and legislative council elections. He further alleged that the political strings of these leaders are controlled from elsewhere, in an apparent reference to Owaisi-led All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen's recent alliance with Nagina MP Chandra Shekhar Aazad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. "Since the BJP lost, I see several political tourists arriving. They have become loudspeakers for someone else's microphone," he said. Referring to the recent Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections, Yadav hailed the victory of Samajwadi Party-backed Akash Agarwal from Agra, alleging that the entire administrative machinery was employed to defeat the candidate. Agarwal was humiliated and subjected to the worst of abuses, but he still emerged victorious, he said, asserting that those who have faced injustice and humiliation are the strength of the 'PDA'. Accusing the BJP government of playing with the future of young people, Yadav claimed that question papers of more than 20 public examinations had been leaked in Uttar Pradesh, leading to their cancellation. He alleged that the government was bent on depriving the youth of employment and reservation opportunities. Yadav also claimed that the BJP government had shut down 26,000 primary schools where children from poor and Dalit families studied. "The government is shutting down schools and opening liquor shops," he jibed, adding that the closures had also affected government teaching jobs. Raising the issue of representation in higher education institutions, Yadav alleged that Dalits and backward classes were not getting adequate opportunities in these institutions. He also criticised the condition of government hospitals, claiming that patients were referred to private hospitals when they failed to receive treatment at government facilities. Yadav alleged that crimes against women, too, were on the rise under BJP rule. He said a Samajwadi Party government would establish the rule of law and ensure social justice. It would also improve the police and emergency response mechanisms to ensure timely justice for the poor. Describing the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections as a contest between five per cent and 95 per cent of the population, Yadav alleged that the BJP had exacerbated people's suffering over the past decade. Referring to the agitation by candidates during the ongoing assistant teachers' recruitment drive over reservation, he said a Samajwadi Party government would ensure that they received their due. "This time, the lathi will lose and the laptop will win. The youth want to study and progress, but attempts are being made to intimidate them," he said.

Mohan Kumar Maharana, a teacher at Sarsapeta Primary School in the Duba area of Kandhamal, had been missing for 15 days after heavy rainfall and a massive landslide triggered by Cyclone Arnab on October 29. He was returning from school when the landslide struck near Dangesi village, trapping him in the forested hillside. “As a young goat herder had ventured into the forest with his animals, he heard a faint voice coming from the area. On approaching the spot, he found Maharana lying in an extremely weak condition on a rock inside the ravine. The herder immediately alerted the villagers and police,” said Raikia police station officer-in-charge A Swarnalata Patra, who led the rescue operation along with police personnel and local villagers. As the hillside gave way near Dangesi village, residents fled towards safer locations, but Maharana became separated from the others. In the darkness and confusion, he slipped into a deep ditch or ravine. With no one around to hear his cries for help, he remained stranded in the forest, unable to find a way out. Continuous rainfall, flooding and the absence of mobile network connectivity in the area compounded his ordeal. His cries gradually weakened as hunger and exhaustion took their toll. Maharana’s wife said her husband struggled to survive in the forest for several days. “He drank muddy water collected in the ditch and from nearby streams to quench his thirst. He also managed to eat whatever edible things he could find in the forest. At one stage, he became so physically weak that he could no longer attempt to escape,” she said. After he went missing, his family approached Raikia police station, where a missing-person complaint was lodged on November 5. Police also alerted residents of neighbouring villages, asking them to report any information about the teacher. “We tried calling him on his mobile phone but knew it would be futile, considering the area has patchy mobile network coverage and his phone would have run out of battery in the rain,” his wife said. Although the goat herder found Maharana, bringing him out of the ravine was a formidable challenge. Rescuers had to trek nearly seven to eight kilometres through dense forest and difficult hilly terrain. They eventually carried him out on a makeshift stretcher fashioned from a wooden pole and a bedsheet. Maharana was taken to Raikia Community Health Centre for treatment. Doctors said prolonged starvation and physical exhaustion had left him extremely weak. He had also suffered cuts and other injuries during the ordeal. His family demanded that he be shifted to Phulbani Medical College and Hospital for better treatment. Officials said Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent landslide had disrupted normal life in Raikia, with residents of affected villages evacuated to government relief shelters, including one at Manikeshwar. “With the school closed and villagers moved to safer locations, the forested surroundings remained largely deserted, which is why no one could find him for so long,” Patra said. The landslide near Dangesi also killed three members of a family, including a nine-month-old boy, when their hilltop house was buried under debris. In neighbouring Ganjam district, Cyclone Arnab triggered another landslide in Gidipabali village, where five bodies were recovered after an extensive search. The district administration on Monday suspended search and rescue operations after families of six missing persons submitted written requests asking officials to stop the operation. They said their houses and family members could be buried under massive rocks and debris at an estimated depth of around 30 feet. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Debabrata Mohanty Debabrata Mohanty is a senior assistant editor of Hindustan Times who works as state correspondent from Odisha covering the state's politics, governance, public policy, natural disasters, environment and its society for close to three decades. With his long years of reporting from the state capital of Bhubaneswar, Mohanty has been known as one of the most experienced and credible journalists covering Odisha for the national English dailies. His reporting combines on-ground detail with deep institutional knowledge detailing the state's changing politics, governance issues, administrative reforms and the functioning of its public institutions. He has regularly reported on issues ranging from legislative developments and public policy implementation. Politics is his core areas of expertise as he closely tracks Odisha's political landscape, including the rise and transformation of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Biju Janata Dal (BJD), the two principal political parties in Odisha. His long association with the state's political establishment enables him to write on contemporary developments in a larger political context. Mohanty takes a deep interest in writing human interest stories, environmental issues and documenting the impact of cyclones, floods, heatwaves, and other climate-related events in one of the most disaster-prone states. His coverage extends to public health, governance reforms and stories on accountability of government institutions. Before joining Hindustan Times, Mohanty worked with The Indian Express, Mail Today, and The Telegraph, where he covered at least six general elections and as many assembly elections. A history sheeter in Bengal's Birbhum district was killed in a police encounter on Sunday afternoon, police said. The deceased has been identified as Ratan Sheikh and had allegedly opened fire and injured a police constable two days ago while police tried to arrest him shortly after his release on bail in one of the cases, district police officers said.

The deceased has been identified as Ratan Sheikh and had allegedly opened fire and injured a police constable two days ago while police tried to arrest him shortly after his release on bail in one of the cases, district police officers said. Sheikh was charged in 36 criminal cases, police said. "Ratan Sheikh, a man with a long criminal history, was found during a manhunt ordered by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari who visited the injured constable, Biswajit Das, at the Burdwan Medical College and Hospital on Saturday," a Birbhum district police officer said, requesting anonymity. Also read: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi after Italian leader raises 'vote chor' slogan: 'Who laughs when India is insulted' A second officer, requesting anonymity, said that police traced Sheikh on Sunday and interrogated him to locate the pistol he used on Saturday. He led the police to Nanoor where the pistol was kept near a bridge but suddenly opened fire with it. The officer said, "The bullets hit a police vehicle. The police team returned fire in self-defence and Sheikh was hit." Doctors at Bolpur subdivisional hospital declared Sheikh dead and his body was taken to the morgue. Sheikh is the fifth criminal to have been killed in a police encounter in West Bengal since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in May. Of the four men who died earlier, three were accused in rape and murder of minor girls, while one was the prime suspect in the murder of a BJP worker. Constable Biswajit Das was shot in the leg during a raid at the Layekbazar bus stand in the Santiniketan police station area of Bolpur on Friday when he went there to arrest Sheikh in connection with one of the 36 cases.

news.headline: Assam to restrict construction in flood-prone areas under proposed zoning law: CM
news.story_lead: Assam to restrict construction in flood-prone areas under proposed zoning law: CM The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month The Assam government plans to bring the floodplains of the Brahmaputra and Barak river basins under a legal land-use zoning system to restrict and regulate construction in vulnerable areas, Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Sunday. The move aims to address the risks posed by unregulated development in flood-prone areas. The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month.
news.full_article_text: Assam to restrict construction in flood-prone areas under proposed zoning law: CM The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month The Assam government plans to bring the floodplains of the Brahmaputra and Barak river basins under a legal land-use zoning system to restrict and regulate construction in vulnerable areas, Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Sunday. The move aims to address the risks posed by unregulated development in flood-prone areas. The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month. Sarma wrote on X: “Flood management begins with understanding our rivers. The Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, provides for scientific mapping of the Brahmaputra and Barak basins and clearly defined flood zones to protect communities and guide safer development.” The proposed legislation envisages using LiDAR technology and satellite imagery to map flood-prone areas across the two river basins. Based on this mapping, the government plans to classify land into three categories: prohibited, regulated and unregulated, with different restrictions on construction and development in each zone. River channels and areas of active flow would fall under the prohibited zone, where construction would not be allowed. Development in regulated zones would be subject to conditions such as elevated plinths and flood-resilient building designs, while normal development would be permitted in unregulated areas outside the identified flood lines. The proposed zoning system would add a land-use regulation mechanism to the state’s existing flood-control measures, which include embankments, riverbank protection, river-training works and drainage improvements. While these measures seek to protect settlements and infrastructure from floodwaters and erosion, the proposed law aims to regulate construction in areas exposed to flooding. Floodplain zoning has featured in Assam’s disaster-management planning before. The Assam State Disaster Management Plan, 2022, called for a regulatory framework to demarcate vulnerable areas and manage construction in floodplains. The proposed Bill seeks to give that planning a legal framework. The draft also envisages setting up Flood Zoning Authorities at different administrative levels to oversee its implementation. During a review of the draft on November 5, Sarma directed officials to ensure that lawful existing property owners were protected. He also stressed the need to safeguard the interests of Scheduled Tribe and Scheduled Caste communities traditionally residing along riverbanks. The proposed framework provides for a 60-day period for public hearings and objections, as well as online and physical mechanisms to appeal against zoning decisions. It also includes safeguards for existing property owners. The need for a broader approach to flood management has been underlined by the scale of this year’s floods. According to the state government’s November 5 review, floods in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat in July claimed 104 lives. The government has said the initiative could be financed through externally aided projects and grants, without imposing an additional financial burden on the state. Sarma has also expressed hope of securing central assistance, including through the Union ministry of Jal Shakti.

On October 12 or 13, they allegedly planted a timer bomb supplied by Shah, but it failed to explode due to a technical malfunction. The third attempt, on November 3, resulted in the explosion around 9.45 pm. A team led by IPS officer Nitin Chaudhary and ATS Bikaner unit in-charge Surendra Kumar coordinated with Punjab Counter Intelligence and Gurdaspur SSP Aditya to apprehend the suspects. "We had earlier arrested a woman named Babita from Gangapur City in a case involving a similar modus operandi, where Pakistani agents allegedly trapped her through romantic overtures. These cases indicate how handlers may be exploiting personal relationships and financial vulnerabilities to recruit women," he told HT. "India is the treasure trove of everyone's hopes. But the state of the world is very strange. For their own selfish reasons, they don't even want India to become great. India moves forward; efforts are underway to create divisions by magnifying smaller identities and provoking conflict among people—tactics he compared to those used during British rule," the RSS Sarsanghchalak said. Urging society to remain united, Bhagwat stressed the need to shed selfishness, petty differences, and ego while building an organised life rooted in Dharma and national service. "Citing the Mahabharata, he noted that despite having a larger force of 11 Akshauhinis and stalwarts like Bhishma, Dronacharya, Karna, and Ashwatthama, the Kauravas lost because of internal discord. In contrast, the Pandavas won with seven Akshauhinis because they stayed united and resolved disputes to preserve harmony," he said. Highlighting the importance of grassroots leadership, Bhagwat said society follows trusted elders and role models. He stated that every village, street, and neighbourhood needs 25 to 100 selfless individuals of pure character who stand with people in times of joy and sorrow and are dedicated to the country. Referring to the principle that actions shape habits, habits shape nature, and nature builds character, he remarked that character is true strength. Speaking on the significance of the RSS Ghosh programme, Bhagwat traced the tradition of battlefield music to ancient texts like the Bhagavad Gita, citing the blowing of sacred conches such as Panchajanya and Devadatta. He noted that although early volunteers initially learned band tunes from British military bands, a sense of self-respect inspired them to create original martial compositions based on Indian classical music theory. He added that RSS band performers do not play for personal praise or applause, but to inculcate discipline, selflessness, teamwork, and a sense of collective progress.

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Sunday stated that attempts are being made to divide India by magnifying smaller identities and inciting internal conflict, comparing such efforts to the divide-and-rule politics of British rule.

Addressing the 'Maru Ninad-2026' Ghosh Shivir organised by the RSS Jodhpur Prant at Rajaram Ashram in Shikarpura, Bhagwat remarked that while India is moving in the right direction today, certain global forces do not want the nation to become great.

"India is the treasure trove of everyone's hopes. But the state of the world is very strange. For their own selfish reasons, they don't even want India to become great. India moves forward; efforts are underway to create divisions by magnifying smaller identities and provoking conflict among people—tactics he compared to those used during British rule," the RSS Sarsanghchalak said.
Urging society to remain united, Bhagwat stressed the need to shed selfishness, petty differences, and ego while building an organised life rooted in Dharma and national service.

news.headline: Uttarakhand MLA loses temper, vandalises stage after he was denied chance to speak at event; booked
news.story_lead: Uttarakhand MLA loses temper, vandalises stage after he was denied chance to speak at event; booked The chief minister lashed out at the Congress, saying it has lost its ground which is causing its members to “lose their mental balance”. Congress MLA Harish Dhami was on Sunday booked for allegedly vandalising a stage after he was "denied" an opportunity to speak in the presence of Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, even as a war of words erupted between the BJP and the Congress over the incident at a prominent fair. The chief minister lashed out at the Congress, saying it has lost its ground which is causing its members to "lose their mental balance", while MLA Harish Dhami called the CM "darpok (coward)", accusing him of suppressing people's voice, and challenged the BJP leader to contest against him.
news.full_article_text: Uttarakhand MLA loses temper, vandalises stage after he was denied chance to speak at event; booked The chief minister lashed out at the Congress, saying it has lost its ground which is causing its members to “lose their mental balance”. Congress MLA Harish Dhami was on Sunday booked for allegedly vandalising a stage after he was "denied" an opportunity to speak in the presence of Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, even as a war of words erupted between the BJP and the Congress over the incident at a prominent fair. The chief minister lashed out at the Congress, saying it has lost its ground which is causing its members to "lose their mental balance", while MLA Harish Dhami called the CM "darpok (coward)", accusing him of suppressing people's voice, and challenged the BJP leader to contest against him. Also read: Bengal police shoots dead ‘criminal’ who allegedly opened fire at cop two days ago; fifth encounter in 6 months The Congress said it stands strongly with its MLA "in the fight for the respect of its public representatives and the rights of the people". Insult to the opposition representatives through the administration will not be tolerated at any cost, state Congress president Ganesh Godiyal said. On Saturday, MLA Harish Dhami allegedly threw microphones and chairs on the stage after the chief minister left the venue and alleged that his mic was switched off as he was speaking. An FIR under relevant sections of the BNS was lodged against the Dharchula MLA and five others for vandalising the inauguration stage of Jauljibi Fair on Saturday following a complaint by Harendra Singh Negi, an officer at the Jauljibi police station. Also read: Punjab woman, accomplice held in Rajasthan train track blast; police suspect ISI's 'romance' strategy to recruit women The FIR has been filed under BNS sections 121 (voluntarily causing hurt ), 132 (assault to deter public servant from discharge of duty), 191(2) (rioting), 324(2) (property damage), and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace), according to Negi. Reacting to the incident, Dhami said, "Congress has crossed all boundaries of anarchy in every sphere, so this episode is also an example of the fact that in the coming days, public is going to reject them completely. "The Congress party has lost its ground, causing its members to lose their mental balance." "A behaviour that we would not even expect from a child is being displayed by Congress leaders, which is unheard of in a democracy... the same approach is followed by their leaders in Delhi.... Public is watching everything...," the CM told reporters in Dehradun. Hitting back, the Congress MLA said, "Till now people had heard that the CM is dhadak Dhami, but he is darpok Dhami." Also read: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi after Italian leader raises 'vote chor' slogan: 'Who laughs when India is insulted' In a social media post on Saturday, MLA Harish Dhami said that he wanted to raise two issues with the government: the death of an eight-year-old girl in the region two days before, and concerns regarding road connectivity in Kanar. He added that it is "deeply unfortunate that an elected representative was denied the opportunity to present the grievances" of their own constituents on the stage at the Jauljibi Fair. "Suppressing voices does not make questions disappear, and switching off a microphone cannot silence the voice of the people! Raising issues -- such as the Kanhar road, basic infrastructure in the region, and long-pending development projects -- before the Chief Minister is my duty, not a crime," said MLA Dhami. He added that the BJP government must understand that in a democracy, "asking questions is not an act of opposition; it is the right of the people". The Congress MLA said that he made mistakes on the stage and apologised to the residents of his constituency. "I have neither learnt to be afraid nor to bow down. If I am wrong, then I will admit it… which is why I challenge the chief minister to contest elections from Dharchula in 2027, and, if my party allows, then I will contest from any constituency where the CM contests from," said the Congress MLA. "While pressure from those in power may stifle voices temporarily, it cannot halt our struggle for issues that serve the public interest. We will neither be intimidated, nor bow down, nor remain silent. Our fight for the rights, dignity, and entitlements of the people of Dharchula will continue with full strength on every platform." Answer the people's questions. Do not attempt to suppress their voice, he added. On Sunday, BJP workers protested against Harish Dhami in Dharchula, burning his effigy and shouting slogans against him. BJP state spokesperson Mathura Dutt Joshi launched a scathing attack on the Congress and said, "The true tactics, character, and face of the Congress have once again been exposed before the public." "Even if the MLA harboured any grievances or complaints, there is no place for such indecent language and improper conduct in public life. The BJP firmly demands that the Congress party issue an immediate public apology for this disgraceful behaviour by its MLA." Joshi alleged that such actions reflect the unruly and anarchic culture of the Congress, adding that the vigilant people of 'Devbhoomi' will never forgive "such inappropriate attitude and arrogance" from their elected representatives. Meanwhile, state Congress president Godiyal justified the anger of party MLA Harish Dhami. "The undemocratic attitude has been shown by Chief Minister Dhami ji. Not giving an opportunity to an elected local public representative to speak from the stage in a historic programme of his own assembly constituency and getting his mic switched off is a completely undemocratic and condemnable act," said Godiyal. He said that violating the protocol is an insult to the MLA and is also an insult to the people there. "Protocol has been openly ignored in the Jauljibi fair. Opposition MLAs and public representatives are not being given due respect by the government and administration, which is against healthy democratic traditions. Efforts to suppress the voice of the public are a threat to democracy," said Godiyal. The state Congress president added that MLA Harish Dhami wanted to present the "burning problems of the area" and the demands of the local people before the chief minister.

news.headline: PM Modi, Trump to join ASEAN Summit in Manila; global conflicts, maritime, economic ties on agenda
news.story_lead: PM Modi, Trump to join ASEAN Summit in Manila; global conflicts, maritime, economic ties on agenda Modi will travel to Manila on November 16 to participate in the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit the following day. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Manila on Monday for a three-day trip to attend the annual India-ASEAN Summit, which is expected to focus on strengthening maritime security ties and expanding economic and commercial partnerships. US President Donald Trump, Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney are also expected to attend the summit.
news.full_article_text: PM Modi, Trump to join ASEAN Summit in Manila; global conflicts, maritime, economic ties on agenda Modi will travel to Manila on November 16 to participate in the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit the following day. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Manila on Monday for a three-day trip to attend the annual India-ASEAN Summit, which is expected to focus on strengthening maritime security ties and expanding economic and commercial partnerships. US President Donald Trump, Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney are also expected to attend the summit. What's on PM Modi's agenda Modi will travel to Manila on November 16 to participate in the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit the following day, on the margins of the ASEAN Summit being hosted by the Philippines. He is also expected to join the leaders of Australia, Japan and the US for a Quad Leaders’ Summit and hold several bilateral meetings. Throughout the India-ASEAN and East Asia summits, New Delhi is looking to boost naval and maritime coordination among like-minded Indo-Pacific states. What is ASEAN ASEAN or the Association of Southeast Asian Nations is one of the most significant geopolitical blocs in the region. The group primarily comprises Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia and East Timor. New Delhi will be joining major global powers, including Washington, Beijing, Tokyo and Canberra, as an official dialogue partner. Prominent world leaders to gather in Manila Global delegations have steadily arrived in the country ahead of the main event, with representatives from ASEAN member states, dialogue partners and international organisations preparing for a packed itinerary of high-level meetings from November 15 to November 17, according to Philippine News Agency. The three-day summit, which includes scheduled talks with world leaders, including US President Donald Trump, will focus on conflicts, including the war in Myanmar, The Associated Press reported citing drafts of post-summit communiques. Trump, Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Canada’s Carney and Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov also feature on the roster for November 17. What's on agenda for ASEAN ASEAN has emerged as a central pillar of India’s Act East policy and vision for the Indo-Pacific, and Rudrendra Tandon, secretary (East) in the external affairs ministry, told a media briefing that the 11-member bloc serves as a “locomotive for peace, stability and economic prosperity”. Annual trade between India and ASEAN member states is worth about $122 billion. “India strongly believes that as an Indian Ocean country that abuts this very important Southeast Asian maritime zone, a strong strategic relationship with ASEAN member states, as a collective as well as individually, is good for both of us,” Tandon said. “It will make us more resilient to handle the very rapid geopolitical changes that are taking place around us. news.headline: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
news.story_lead: Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube channel of his lawyer - Published 5 hours ago A candidate who came first in South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam has admitted cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools. news.full_article_text: Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube channel of his lawyer - Published 5 hours ago A candidate who came first in South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam has admitted cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools. Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube account of his lawyer, Lee Don-Ho, adding that he had confessed to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency and offered details on how he cheated. The 34-year-old scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, which initially raised suspicions and sparked online speculation. Standardised national tests play an outsized role in career trajectories for South Koreans, making their results - and efforts to unduly inflate those results - of great importance. "I cheated in both the first and second rounds of the tax account exam by using electronic devices and generative AI," Han said in the video published on Sunday. "I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating." When accusations he had cheated first began to surface, Han had denied any wrongdoing - but said he had changed his mind after thinking about the feelings of the candidate who had come second in the exam. He went on to apologise to the other entrants who had passed the tests fairly. "It seems that because of me, other successful candidates are being suspected," he suggested. The Ministry of Employment and Labour and the Human Resources Development Service held an emergency meeting after Han admitted cheating. The South Korean president's policy chief Ha Jun-kyung said new measures would be introduced to prevent cheating and warned "past crimes" would be "tracked down and apprehended to the very end". Those found to have used AI to cheat in the tax accountancy exam will have their qualification revoked and will be banned from retaking the test for five years, the government said. The scandal comes just days before the east Asian nation's annual college entrance exam, a crucial hurdle for students. Can smart glasses exam cheating be stopped? A series of cases involving exam cheating with AI glasses in South Korea has universities and schools scrambling to rein in the use of the technology. Han said he had only cheated to try and earn money and get a job that would make his parents proud of him again. Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency told Korean news agency Yonhap on Sunday that it was looking into the case. "We received a written confession through the test taker's lawyer this morning regarding cheating on the tax accountant exam," it confirmed in a statement. It added that the case had now been assigned to investigators. Because of the significance of the national exams, instances of cheating are not uncommon in South Korea, and cases involving the use of AI have become more prominent as the technology becomes more sophisticated. Last month, two college applicants were reported to have used AI glasses to try and cheat their entrance exams at two Seoul universities. Education ministry data also says there were four cases of cheating through AI glasses at middle and high schools in the past 12 months. The National Health Accounts Estimates for India 2023-24, released by the Union Health Ministry, showed that out-of-pocket expenditure as a share of total health expenditure fell from 64.2 per cent in 2013-14 to 42.7 per cent in 2023-24, highlighting a significant transformation in the country's healthcare financing landscape. "Between 2013-14 and 2023-24, government health expenditure increased from approximately ₹ 1.30 lakh crore to ₹ 4.14 lakh crore. "The simultaneous increase in public healthcare financing and decline in the proportion of spending borne directly by households reflect India's progress towards a more accessible, affordable and financially protective healthcare system," the health ministry said in a statement. According to the estimates, the OOPE declined from 43.4 per cent in 2022-23 to 42.7 per cent in 2023-24, indicating a continued reduction in the proportion of healthcare costs directly borne by households. "The sustained downward trend reflects the expanding role of government-supported healthcare services and financial protection mechanisms. "Initiatives aimed at improving access to free and affordable treatment, medicines, diagnostics and hospital services are supporting efforts to reduce dependence on direct household spending," the ministry said. The government's share in total health expenditure also increased by 14.9 percentage points over the decade, the estimates showed, while per capita government health expenditure rose from ₹ 1,042 in 2013-14 to ₹ 2,959 in 2023-24, an increase of nearly three times. The estimates also highlighted a rise in social security expenditure on health, with its share in total health expenditure increasing from 6 per cent in 2013-14 to 11 per cent in 2023-24. This includes government-financed health insurance schemes, such as the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, state insurance schemes, social health insurance and medical expenditure for government employees. Private health insurance expenditure also increased, with its share of total health expenditure rising from 3.4 per cent in 2013-14 to 10.2 per cent in 2023-24, the estimates showed. The government expenditure on primary healthcare stood at around ₹ 1.53 lakh crore in 2023-24, underscoring the increased focus on primary and community-level healthcare, the ministry said. Initiatives such as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, free drugs and diagnostics, the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme, Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana and AMRIT pharmacies have contributed to efforts to improve access to affordable healthcare, it said. According to the ministry, the Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY has also strengthened financial protection by providing cashless hospitalisation benefits to eligible beneficiaries. The NHA Estimates for India 2023-24 constitute the 11th round of estimates prepared by the National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat that operates within the National Health Systems Resource Centre , Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Efforts by Donald Trump to fast-track the confirmation of federal judges have run into opposition within the United States Senate. The last-minute push aimed to secure conservative lifetime appointments across the federal judiciary before the legislative term concluded.

### Intra-Party Roadblocks in the US Senate

- **Legislative Challenges:** Under the US constitutional framework, all presidential nominees for federal judgeships require approval from the Senate.
- **Republican Objections:** Opposition from within Republican ranks has created significant hurdles, preventing several nominees from receiving swift confirmations.
- **Significance:** The resistance underscores intra-party friction regarding the nomination of controversial judicial candidates during transitional or late-stage legislative sessions.

### Overview of Statements and Missile Arsenal Estimates

Recent statements regarding US strategic actions against Iranian military infrastructure have highlighted differing assessments of Iran's residual strike capabilities.

* **Public Claims:** Donald Trump asserted that military strikes conducted by the United States had effectively destroyed Iran's weapons assets.
* **Reported Inventory:** Contrary to claims of complete destruction, assessments indicate that Iran retains a substantial stockpile estimated at 2,500 missiles.
* **Security Implications:** The retention of 2,500 missiles underscores the persistence of Iran's missile program as a central factor in West Asian regional security dynamics and highlights the difficulty of completely neutralizing distributed missile inventories.

news.full_article_text:
### Parliament Winter Session & Proposed Delimitation-Linked Women's Quota Bill

The Union government is preparing to convene the Winter Session of Parliament in the first week of December, placing a major legislative focus on passing a constitutional amendment bill tied to electoral delimitation and women's political representation.

#### Key Objectives & Proposed Provisions
* **Expansion of Lok Sabha Seats**: The legislation seeks to expand the maximum seat capacity of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to up to 850 seats via delimitation.
* **Implementation of Women's Quota**: The structural expansion is intended to facilitate 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures prior to the 2029 general elections.
* **Proposed Delimitation Formula**: The government is examining a formula to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent across all states, while retaining the inter-state seat distribution ratio established under the 1971 Census to address regional demographic concerns, particularly from southern states.

#### Numerical Dynamics in Lok Sabha
* **Special Majority Requirement**: A Constitution Amendment Bill requires a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, amounting to 361 votes in a full 543-member Lok Sabha.
* **Current Strength & Vacancies**: The Lok Sabha currently has 540 members due to 3 existing vacancies.
* **Coalition Position**: The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) holds 320 members and requires opposition support to cross the 361-vote mark. Government sources anticipate securing the bill with a margin of 15 to 18 votes.
* **Previous Vote Outcome**: An earlier attempt to pass the legislation during a special sitting on April 17 failed to achieve the necessary votes.

#### Procedural Status of the Previous Session
* **Unprorogued Record**: The previous Monsoon Session was adjourned sine die on August 13 and remained unprorogued for 94 days, breaking the previous record of 87 days established in 2008.
* **Notice Rules**: Under parliamentary rules, an extended sitting of an unprorogued session can be called with a minimum of 2 days' notice, whereas summoning a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.
* **Constitutional Standard**: The Constitution does not specify a fixed timeline for the President to prorogue a House after it is adjourned sine die.

#### Political Challenges & Friction
* Opposition parties are conducting campaigns against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, signaling potential disruptions during the upcoming session.

* **विशेष बहुमत की आवश्यकता**: संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पारित करने के लिए उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों के दो-तिहाई बहुमत की आवश्यकता होती है, जो 543 सदस्यीय लोकसभा में 361 वोट बैठता है।
* **वर्तमान सदस्य संख्या**: 3 रिक्तियों के कारण वर्तमान में लोकसभा सदस्यों की संख्या 540 है।
* **गठबंधन की स्थिति**: सत्तारूढ़ एनडीए के पास 320 सदस्य हैं और उसे 361 के आंकड़े तक पहुंचने के लिए विपक्ष के समर्थन की आवश्यकता होगी। हालांकि, सरकारी सूत्रों को 15 से 18 वोटों के अंतर से विधेयक पारित होने का भरोसा है।
* **पिछला प्रयास**: इससे पहले 17 अप्रैल को आयोजित एक विशेष बैठक के दौरान यह विधेयक आवश्यक संख्याबल न जुटा पाने के कारण पारित नहीं हो सका था।

#### पिछले सत्र की प्रक्रियात्मक स्थिति
* **सत्रावसान न होने का रिकॉर्ड**: पिछला मानसून सत्र 13 अगस्त को अनिश्चित काल के लिए स्थगित (sine die) कर दिया गया था और 94 दिनों तक सत्रावसान (prorogue) नहीं हुआ, जिसने 2008 के 87 दिनों के रिकॉर्ड को तोड़ दिया।
* **नोटिस से जुड़े नियम**: संसदीय नियमों के तहत, अनिश्चित काल के लिए स्थगित सत्र की विस्तारित बैठक केवल 2 दिनों के नोटिस पर बुलाई जा सकती है, जबकि नया सत्र बुलाने के लिए कम से कम 14 दिनों के नोटिस की आवश्यकता होती है।
* **संवैधानिक प्रावधान**: भारतीय संविधान में अनिश्चित काल के लिए स्थगन के बाद राष्ट्रपति द्वारा सत्र के सत्रावसान के लिए कोई निश्चित समय सीमा निर्धारित नहीं है।

#### राजनीतिक चुनौतियां
* विपक्षी दल मतदाता सूचियों के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) के खिलाफ अभियान चला रहे हैं और मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग कर रहे हैं, जिससे आगामी सत्र में हंगामे के आसार हैं।

news.headline: Cockroach Janta Party Announces Zonal Leadership and State Coordination Committees
news.story_lead: The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced key zonal leadership appointments and constituted coordination committees across 10 states and regions to expand its grassroots setup. As part of its structural expansion, the organization named zonal in-charges for the West and North zones alongside state-level bodies of varying sizes.
news.full_article_text:
### Zonal Appointments and Structural Expansion

In a strategic effort to expand its organizational footprint, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced the creation of zonal leadership roles and coordination committees across 10 states and regions on Saturday.

Key zonal appointments include:
- **West Zone In-Charge:** Kshitij Pagar
- **North Zone In-Charge:** Dr. Vivek Sangwan
- **North Zone Coordination Committee Members:** Muhammad Junaid and Geegraj Jorli

### Composition of State Coordination Committees

To manage regional activities and enhance grassroots engagement, CJP established coordination committees with varying membership sizes across ten jurisdictions:
- **Uttar Pradesh:** 16 members
- **Maharashtra:** 15 members
- **Jharkhand:** 14 members
- **Northeast Region:** 14 members
- **Bihar:** 13 members
- **West Bengal:** 12 members
- **Haryana:** 6 members
- **Uttarakhand:** 6 members
- **Rajasthan:** 5 members
- **Jammu and Kashmir:** 4 members

### Background and Past Agitations

Founded by Abhijeet Dipke in May 2026, the CJP originated as a satirical digital platform in response to public remarks by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant concerning unemployed youth. It gradually evolved into a student and youth mobilization movement focusing on paper leaks, employment issues, and systemic examination reforms.

 major actions by the group include a 36-day protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar regarding the NEET-UG paper leak case, demanding political accountability which preceded the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25. The outfit has also raised concerns regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and participated in the opposition alliance's rally in Delhi on November 1.

hindi_translation.story_lead: युवा केंद्रित संगठन कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) ने अपने संगठनात्मक विस्तार के तहत 10 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में जोनल प्रभारियों की नियुक्ति की है और समन्वय समितियों का गठन किया है। संगठन ने पश्चिमी और उत्तरी जोन के लिए प्रभारियों के साथ-साथ विभिन्न राज्यों के लिए समितियों के सदस्यों की घोषणा की।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### आंचलिक नियुक्तियां और संगठनात्मक विस्तार

अपने संगठनात्मक आधार को मजबूत करने के उद्देश्य से कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) ने शनिवार को 10 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में आंचलिक पदों और समन्वय समितियों की स्थापना की घोषणा की।

प्रमुख आंचलिक नियुक्तियां निम्नलिखित हैं:
- **पश्चिम जोन प्रभारी:** क्षितिज पगार
- **उत्तर जोन प्रभारी:** डॉ. विवेक सांगवान
- **उत्तर जोन समन्वय समिति सदस्य:** मोहम्मद जुनैद और गीगराज जोरली

### राज्य समन्वय समितियों का गठन

विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में गतिविधियों के संचालन और जमीनी उपस्थिति बढ़ाने के लिए पार्टी ने 10 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में समन्वय समितियां गठित की हैं:
- **उत्तर प्रदेश:** 16 सदस्य
- **महाराष्ट्र:** 15 सदस्य
- **झारखंड:** 14 सदस्य
- **पूर्वोत्तर क्षेत्र:** 14 सदस्य
- **बिहार:** 13 सदस्य
- **पश्चिम बंगाल:** 12 सदस्य
- **हरियाणा:** 6 सदस्य
- **उत्तराखंड:** 6 सदस्य
- **राजस्थान:** 5 सदस्य
- **जम्मू और कश्मीर:** 4 सदस्य

### पृष्ठभूमि और प्रमुख प्रदर्शन

अभिजीत दिपके द्वारा मई 2026 में स्थापित CJP की शुरुआत एक व्यंग्यात्मक ऑनलाइन अभियान के रूप में हुई थी। यह भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्य कांत द्वारा बेरोजगार युवाओं को लेकर की गई टिप्पणी के बाद शुरू हुआ था। बाद में यह परीक्षा धांधली और युवा बेरोजगारी के मुद्दों पर ध्यान केंद्रित करने वाले आंदोलन में बदल गया।

संगठन ने NEET-UG पेपर लीक मामले को लेकर दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर पर 36 दिनों का विरोध प्रदर्शन आयोजित किया था, जिसके बाद तत्कालीन शिक्षा मंत्री धर्मेंद्र प्रधान ने 25 जुलाई को इस्तीफा दे दिया था। इसके अतिरिक्त, संगठन ने मतदाता सूची के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) का विरोध करते हुए मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग भी की है।
